fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Walkway; Access Drive; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders can distinguish it from neighboring driveways at night or in low visibility.
• Trim trees and shrubs along the access drive so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so fire apparatus and ambulances can reach both structures.
• Post visible unit or structure identifiers on both the main residence and the detached structure so responders can orient quickly on arrival.
• Clear a path around the detached structure so responders can move between it and the main residence on foot without pushing through dense vegetation.
• Thin vegetation between the two structures so responders have a clear line of sight from one to the other.
• Identify a parking or staging area near the access drive entrance that does not block the drive for additional responding units.
• If a rear gate or fence limits access to the rear of the property, keep it unlocked or install a Knox-compatible lock so responders can reach the back of both structures.
• Mark or communicate to local dispatch that this property has a single access point with two structures so responding units can plan accordingly.

wildfire.conditions: Large Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Green Space; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Grass Cover; Multiple Access Routes; Vegetation Along Driveway
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees growing close to the structure to increase the gap between the tree canopy and the building.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to reduce the amount of connected plant material that could carry fire toward the building.
• Remove any dead branches or dead material from large trees near the structure.
• Clear grass and low ground cover growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Keep grass in open areas mowed short, particularly where it connects the open space to trees or structures.
• Trim overhanging branches along the driveway to keep both access routes clear for vehicles.
• Remove or cut back shrubs and low vegetation growing along the driveway edge that could block vehicle movement.
• Separate any scattered trees from nearby shrubs or tall grass by clearing the low vegetation growing beneath and around them.
• Keep the ground beneath large trees clear of fallen branches, dead leaves, and accumulated plant debris.
• Maintain the open green space by keeping grass cut low so it does not connect taller vegetation to the structure.
